findings.statement: Engine::edit_source has no production caller, yet it keeps a hand copy of each edit_param phase: guard re-elaboration, solver resolution, wave-2, post-wave2 reseed and collection resize. 301 non-comment lines sit in matching runs of 6 or more lines between the two (31% of edit_param's code, 37% of edit_source's). The longest run is the 96-line solver-resolution block. The copies are linked only by 'Paired with … change them together' / 'mirrors' comments, and they have already diverged in at least four places. (a) Post-wave2 reseed: task #4707 (d248baef96) relaxed edit_param's reseed to the full demanded downstream cone and added the same cone pass to cold eval (engine_eval.rs 'Task #4707: cold driver-ordered guarded-member downstream cone'). edit_source's copy is still 'BOUNDED to members ∩ demand — no downstream cone (matches cold semantics)', so its comment is now false. (b) Wave-2: edit_param's is guard-aware and deactivates inactive members. edit_source's still evaluates the default_expr of every wave-2 cell, which is the shape edit_param's comment gives as the reason the legacy wave was retired. (c) Eval contexts: edit_source's Phase 1 members, post-wave2 active members and collection-resize cells use eval_ctx_with_meta without determinacy or containment (4 sites). edit_param uses cell_eval_ctx there (INV-EVAL-2). This is forced by structure: PendingWarmSeedsGuard holds &mut self.warm_pool from line 3328 to line 4583, so `self` cannot serve as the ContainmentQuery. (d) Journaling: edit_source's post-wave2 active member and its collection-resize cells use bare values and snapshot inserts with no journal. edit_param routes both through commit_cell_result with CacheLeg::Skip (INV-EVAL-1).
findings.proposal: Decide what edit_source is for. If no consumer is planned, delete it with its 15 test files' calls and its instrumentation fields (last_role_flip_probes, last_diff_value_cells). If it stays, move the post-eval phases into shared methods that take an explicit structural context (reverse index, trace map, demand), and scope PendingWarmSeedsGuard so it no longer spans those phases. Then both entries run one copy with cell_eval_ctx.
findings.next_change: A plausible next change is a fix to one edit-path phase: say the next INV-EVAL-1 migration, or a guard-semantics change like #4707 applied to edit_param. To do it correctly the agent must know that edit_source carries a twin of that phase. It has to find the twin through 'Paired with'/'mirrors' prose, then adapt it to new_reverse_index/new_trace_map/new_demand and to the warm_pool borrow that rules out cell_eval_ctx. Only edit_source's own integration tests and the differential harness would catch a missed twin. No production path runs edit_source, so the drift ships silently, as it did with #4707.

findings.statement: Engine::edit_param is the production warm-edit path (reify-cli mcp_context.rs, GUI param edits). It is one 1938-line function: 883 comment lines and 977 code lines, brace depth 9, approximate decision count 115. It runs eight banner-delimited phases in sequence: main walk, composed fields, guard re-elaboration, resolution, resolution reseed, post-wave2 reseed, collection resize with forall re-elaboration, and realization eviction. They communicate through 28 function-scope locals, 12 of them `let mut` (values, new_snapshot, skipped, has_changed_parent, diagnostics, structural_mutation, phase1_reelaborated, …), each alive from its declaration to the return. The prose is mostly task provenance and review defence (142 comment lines cite task numbers; 31 are review-round or amend narratives, e.g. 'Verified (reviewer amend, round 2): a repo-wide grep…'), not a contract the next agent needs.
findings.proposal: Turn the eight phases into named methods over an explicit edit-transaction value. The value would own new_snapshot, values and the sinks, and each phase would return what the next one reads (phase1_reelaborated, structural_mutation, resolved ids). Move the provenance and review prose into commit messages or the PRD.
findings.next_change: The next edit-path change, for example a new eval-phase capability like a ninth back-prop leg, or a fix to how guard re-elaboration interacts with the collection resize. The agent must load all 1938 lines and work out which of the 12 mutable locals each later phase reads. It must also take on trust prose that is often stale (it cites line numbers such as ':1325-1331' and 'engine_edit.rs:845' that no longer match the code). Per-phase tests in unified_dag_edit_path.rs and the in-file commit-primitive pins catch some wrong versions. Nothing catches a phase that reads a local an earlier phase has left half-updated.

findings.statement: The 'Warm-Resolution back-prop' contract is held in a 109-line module-doc roster at the top of engine_edit.rs (lines 26-134). It lists six arms across engine_eval.rs and engine_edit.rs and, for each, which of eight legs it writes, and it ends with the instruction 'Check all eight legs when modifying'. No primitive enforces this. Each arm hand-rolls the solve loop and its SolveResult handling: the literal 'Constraint solver made no progress' appears at 6 code sites (engine_edit.rs ×2, engine_eval.rs ×4), and 'resolved via auto(free)' at 5. The leg differences between arms (journal vs no journal, resolved_params written or not, objective_provenance only on eval) live only in prose, so the doc has needed its own correction commits (56badf0b7c, 561d645fd6).
findings.proposal: Introduce one resolution write-back primitive (solve outcome to commits plus diagnostics plus resolved-id set), with the per-arm leg differences passed as explicit policy values, the same way CacheLeg does it for cell commits. Then shrink the roster to a pointer.
findings.next_change: Say the agent adds objective_provenance to eval_cached, or adds a ninth leg such as a new per-resolution cache field. It must read the roster, then find six arms by function name in engine_eval.rs (about 10k lines) and engine_edit.rs, and edit each one. Per-arm RED/GREEN pins (e.g. edit_param_recorded_sites_route_through_commit_primitive) catch a regression only on arms that already have a pin. Nothing catches an arm missing a leg that has no pin.

findings.statement: Three rules that change what a name resolves to are passed through thread-local ambient sets installed by RAII guards, not through arguments. They are RESOLUTION_ENUM_NAMES (EnumNameScope), RESOLUTION_SHADOWING_ENUM_NAMES (LocalEnumShadowScope) and ALIAS_DEFER_IN_PROGRESS (AliasDeferScope). Each is justified as avoiding a signature change across '~100 call sites'. The measured production callers outside the file are 23 for resolve_type_expr_with_aliases and 6 for _kinded. Whether a resolution sees enum names depends on whether some caller up the stack installed the scope: temporal coupling the call does not show. The doc lists the install sites ('installed … at exactly four sites'; 'Keep this list in sync: grep … is the authority'). That list is already stale: validate_pub_parametric_alias_def_site in the same file became a fifth production site in 77c80cdcfb (2026-09-19). The doc had already been corrected once before that (c48d38a698, 2026-09-01). That function also receives enum_names as an explicit parameter and re-installs it ambiently just so a callee can read it. A missing install has already caused a silent warning-to-error regression (esc-5429-1, recorded in the doc).
findings.proposal: Put the alias registry, structure/trait/enum name sets, the shadow set and the in-progress set into one ResolutionCtx passed by reference. That is one mechanical signature change at about 55 sites, and it removes all three ambient channels and their prose.
findings.next_change: A fourth context-dependent rule, say a module-local trait shadowing a prelude structure, or per-phase visibility. Following the established pattern, the agent adds a fourth thread_local and scope, then has to find every phase that must install it, using a doc list that is already wrong. A wrong version is caught only by a behavioural test of that exact shape. A phase that forgets the install silently resolves the name another way.

findings.statement: Type-expression resolution varies on two independent axes: substitution or not, and full Type vs DimensionVector result. Each combination has its own hand-written function: resolve_type_alias_expr, resolve_type_alias_expr_with_subst, resolve_type_alias_expr_to_dimension and resolve_type_alias_expr_to_dim_with_subst, plus the builtin pair resolve_parameterized_builtin_type and resolve_parameterized_builtin_type_with_subst. The 12-name parameterized-builtin table is therefore written four times: is_parameterized_builtin_name, two independent 12-arm `match name` blocks, and the drift-guard test list. The two builtin matchers have diverged. The base resolver's Scalar, Vector3 and Point3 arms classify dimension-param slots (classify_dim_slot, about 30 lines each, emitting DimParamKind). The subst variant's arms go straight to the dimension resolver. The drift test pins only the predicate's name set, so an arm added to or changed in one matcher is not caught in the other.
findings.proposal: Drive both matchers from one per-constructor table (arity, slot kinds, how to build the Type), with substitution as a parameter of a single resolver rather than a twin function.
findings.next_change: Adding a 13th parameterized builtin (e.g. Quaternion<Q>), or changing dimension-slot handling for one constructor. The agent must edit the predicate, both matchers and the test list, and work out whether the alias-DFS (subst) path needs the base path's DimSlotClass handling. Per-arm resolution tests catch only the path they exercise, so the other matcher can stay wrong.

findings.statement: Geometry builtins are identified by string names that are restated across files. compile_geometry_call_inner is one 1581-line function dispatching on 60 name arms (approximate CCN ~117). The same names appear again in units.rs GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES (65 names), in geometry.rs geometry_arg_indices (35 names, with a silent `_ => &[]` default and a prose 'IMPORTANT … MUST be registered here' warning), in check_profile_preconditions arms, in geometry_traits_inference.rs, in reify-ir GEOMETRY_OP_DESCRIPTORS, and in reify-eval geometry_ops.rs. The reify-ir descriptor table already records which builtins take a geometry argument (parent_role), so geometry_arg_indices restates a fact that has a home. The duplicates are kept consistent by cross-check tests (geometry_arg_indices_consistent_with_descriptor_table, all_dispatch_functions_accounted_for, the traits-inference coverage test). That reconciliation-by-census is the smell, not the cure.
findings.proposal: Key dispatch, arg indices and trait inference off the reify-ir descriptor (or a typed builtin enum parsed once at the call boundary), and split the match into per-family lowering functions selected by descriptor role.
findings.next_change: Adding a geometry builtin (e.g. a variable-radius chamfer). The agent must add a name to GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES, a descriptor row in reify-ir, a geometry_arg_indices entry, an arm inside the 1581-line match, a traits-inference arm and an eval-side handler. The cross-check tests catch a missing arg-index or a dispatch arm once the descriptor row exists. A builtin left out of the descriptor table escapes every check, and the silent `&[]` default breaks let-bound geometry references for it.

findings.statement: Guarded-group member activation is spelled four times with different rules: Engine::eval's third-pass members loop, its near-identical else_members loop, post_solver_re_eval_guard_cells, and eval_guarded_group_param_cell. The third pass routes Param members through eval_guarded_group_param_cell, which honours and validates param_overrides. The post-solver pass, which re-runs whenever a solver is attached, re-evaluates every active Param member from default_expr and never consults param_overrides. Yet the comment at its call site says the pass is 'idempotent with the earlier pass for guards that don't depend on auto params'. Inactive Auto members are written (Undef, Auto) by the third pass but skipped by the post-solver pass. The third pass's Let and Auto arms bypass commit_cell_result entirely, with no cache or journal legs, while its Param arm commits all four legs. eval_cached sidesteps the whole question by falling back to a full eval() for any module with guarded groups (task 5240).
findings.proposal: One `activate_guarded_group(group, guard_value, phase)` that owns the per-kind active/inactive rule (Param via the override-aware path, Let, Auto) and commits through commit_cell_result. The cold third pass, the post-solver pass and a future warm path then all call it.
findings.next_change: The next change touches guarded groups: support on the warm path (removing the task-5240 fallback), a new member kind, or override semantics. The agent must reconcile four activation spellings whose disagreements (overrides, inactive autos, commit legs) are undocumented except by a comment claiming they agree. A guarded Param with a user override in a solver-attached model plausibly loses the override after the post-solve pass. No test in tests/guard_eval.rs combines a param override with a solver.

findings.statement: Handling of a per-scope solve outcome has six hand-maintained arms, and they implement different step sets. The arms are: Engine::eval single-scope, Engine::dispatch_merged_cluster_solve, Engine::eval_cached single-scope, Engine::dispatch_merged_cluster_solve_cached, and engine_edit.rs's edit_param and edit_source solver blocks. Only the two cold arms do these steps: call solve_ranked_with_dispatch and emit W_SOLVER_OPTIMALITY_UNPROVEN, record objective_provenance, run materialize_dependent_cells (the joint-drive write-back its doc calls the PRD section 6.3 PRIMARY INVARIANT), emit E_OBJECTIVE_UNCONSUMED, record undef-cause solve failures, and stamp SnapshotProvenance::Resolution. All four warm/edit arms omit every one of these. The auto(free) non-uniqueness warning has a shared helper (push_merged_cluster_nonunique_warnings) used by 2 arms, while the other 4 inline the identical format string. Solver-value write-back is Started/Completed-journaled on the cold arms and a bare cache record with no journal on eval_cached. governing_objective's doc nevertheless asserts eval and eval_cached build a 'byte-identical solver invariant'. The arms are not copies of one another (code similarity 0.23 to 0.36), so the divergence is in what each arm does, not in its spelling.
findings.proposal: Give 'apply a SolveResult to a scope set' one owner. It takes the problem, solve result, optimality, pinned autos, a WritebackPolicy for cold or warm let re-propagation, and whether to record provenance. It returns the resolved ids and diagnostics. Each arm then varies only by the explicit policy values, so an intentionally absent step is visible as a policy choice rather than a missing line.
findings.next_change: The next change adds a post-solve step, such as a new solve diagnostic, a provenance field, or a fix to the joint-drive write-back. The agent must locate all six arms across engine_eval.rs and engine_edit.rs. For each arm it must also decide whether that step's absence today is intentional or drift; neither file records that, except a prose census in engine_edit.rs's module doc covering journal legs only. A wrong version, meaning the step added to the cold arms only, is caught only if a warm==cold differential row (tests/common/differential.rs is a per-row corpus) happens to exercise that step. Nothing catches it structurally.

findings.statement: reify-compiler's crate root re-exports 28 sibling modules wholesale (`pub(crate) use X::*;`, 5 of them under #[allow(unused_imports)]), and its own comment says this exists 'for internal cross-module access via `use super::*;`'. 25 of the 56 top-level src files begin with `use super::*;`, so every pub(crate) item of 28 modules is in scope, unqualified, in each of them. Reading one file therefore never tells you where its callees live. guards.rs calls 17 crate functions unqualified from 6 different files, traits.rs 12 from 4, forall_elaborate.rs 7 from 4. The mesh also hides a module cycle. entity.rs (8,264 lines) calls guards.rs's compile_block_guard/compile_guarded_members/register_guarded_names/compile_per_decl_guard 6 times. guards.rs calls back into entity.rs's build_param_value_cell_decl, build_auto_let_value_cell_decl, resolve_auto_let_cell_type and fixup_option_none_for_let, which makes guards.rs a satellite of entity.rs rather than a layer under it.
findings.proposal: Replace the crate-root globs with explicit `use crate::<module>::{names}` per file, starting with the slice's leaves (guards, traits, forall_elaborate, geometry_list). Move the param/let cell-builder helpers that guards.rs takes back from entity.rs into a lower module that both import, so the dependency runs one way. Add a check that fails on new `pub(crate) use X::*` lines.
findings.next_change: An agent adding a member kind to guarded blocks edits guards.rs::compile_guarded_members. It must find out where is_geometry_let, build_param_value_cell_decl, compile_expr_guarded, emit_ice_unresolved and extract_solver_hints live and what invariants they assume. Nothing in guards.rs names their modules, so the agent has to search a 22k-line entity.rs/expr.rs pair. A wrong change, such as calling a same-named helper from the wrong module or adding a third mutual call, compiles cleanly. No lint or test reports a new peer cycle.

findings.statement: CompilationScope is a clone-per-lambda/quantifier/match-arm struct with 30 `pub(crate)` fields and thin methods. Other files populate and read it directly: 188 field accesses from 11 files outside scope.rs (expr.rs 105, entity.rs 50, member_path.rs 14, connect.rs 6, ...). Its cross-field invariants are stated in field docs and kept true by callers in other files, not by the type. Examples: 'geometry_list_rejected is disjoint from geometry_list_elements by construction'; 'match_arm_groups.keys() == match_arm_group_arm_member_types.keys() is enforced by an unconditional assert! in compile_entity'; 'populated in the entity.rs Sub pre-pass'; the five sibling sub_* maps 'populated at both Sub pre-pass sites'. That doc prose is 56% of the file.
findings.proposal: Group the sub_* maps into one per-sub record populated by a single constructor from the resolved child template, and make the geometry-list pair a single enum-valued map. Then make fields private behind query methods, so invariants live in the type and the field docs shrink to contracts.
findings.next_change: An agent adding a per-sub fact, say a seventh sub_* sibling map for the next connect check, must find both Sub pre-pass sites in entity.rs, the match-arm cluster fold, and every reader in expr.rs/connect.rs. It also has to keep the 'absence means unknown' contract by convention. Forgetting the match-arm site compiles and silently yields 'unknown' for clusters, as the existing sub_declared_member_names doc already concedes for `where`-block ports.

findings.statement: The reflective purpose-query kind is a closed set of three values ('params', 'geometric_params', 'material_params'), carried as String end to end: in reify-compiler ResolvedSchemaQuery.query_kind, in reify-ir CompiledExprKind::PurposeReflectiveAggregation.query_kind, and through reify-eval's expand_purpose_reflective_placeholders. compile_purpose produces the three resolved queries with an inline Param|Auto plus is_geometric_param_type / is_material_param_type filter. engine_purposes re-implements the same three-way filter as chained string comparisons for its fallback path. findings.statement: commit_cell_result_at encodes whether the cache leg was skipped, which its doc calls 'the journal-only source of truth', by appending `|cache-skip=<reason>` to the Started event's EventPayload::Custom string. findings.statement: stdlib_sources orders 47 stdlib modules by hand. stdlib_topo::compile_modules_topo is a working dependency mechanism keyed on `import` edges, yet no stdlib .ri file declares an import. findings.statement: Sub-component instance cells are elaborated by unfold.rs, a second implementation of cell elaboration parallel to engine_eval.rs's template-scope path. Since 2026-07-06 the two have been reconciled one rule at a time: #5360 cee8ad1415 (nested subs resolved module-only while the top-level path used the prelude fallback), #7418 eaae8530e8/09455b16c1 (child params not visited in dependency order), #5057 49abf75ff6 (determinacy-predicate divergence) and #6662 (@optimized reuse at instance scope). Two divergences remain built in. First, elaborate_child_params_only and elaborate_child_lets_only meet cell_eval_ctx's required `containment` and `runtime_sink` arguments with a `NoContainment` null object (always None, so restricted-field samples become Undef) and a fresh RefCell that is then dropped. The template-scope let walk passes `self` (Engine's ContainmentQuery) and calls store_cell_replay_diagnostics. Second, unfold_recursive_sub evaluates guard and arg expressions with eval_ctx_with_meta, which has no determinacy or diagnostics sink. A further known wrong behaviour is recorded only in the NoContainment doc comment, with no task cite: a recursion-local name resolves its value from child_values but its determinacy from the global snapshot.
findings.proposal: Give instance and template scope one per-cell elaboration primitive, parameterised by the scope projection (value map plus determinacy view), so that containment, diagnostics capture and ordering are supplied once. In the interim, drain the child runtime_sink into `diagnostics`, store it with store_cell_replay_diagnostics, and add a differential test that elaborates one fixture at both scopes.
findings.next_change: Someone adds a runtime warning to a field op, a builtin that depends on containment, or a new param/let elaboration rule on the template path in engine_eval.rs. To get it right they must know that cells inside a `sub` go through unfold.rs instead, and that this path drops runtime diagnostics and containment. Nothing compares a cell elaborated at template scope with the same cell under `sub`. A one-path change is caught only if some fixture happens to nest the construct, which is how each of the four reconciliation fixes was found.

findings.statement: engine_admin.rs (header comment: 'Split from lib.rs (task 2032) — admin methods') is one of 19 files holding `impl Engine` blocks over the private 67-field Engine struct declared in lib.rs. It reads and writes those fields directly rather than through an interface. Its purpose cannot be stated without 'and'. It holds the 67-field struct-literal constructor and five other constructors; the kernel, solver, optimized, compute and morph registries; about 25 state accessors; 28 cfg(test-instrumentation) seams; the shell-GUI mesh decoder (5 fns, about 400 lines); kernel-pin diagnostics; the persistent-cache startup sweep; and undef-cause tracing. Twelve Engine fields named last_* keep per-call results at instance lifetime, and most are read only by cfg-gated accessors (heuristic 5). store_morph_source and morph_source carry `#[allow(dead_code)] // consumed by #4744 step-20`, yet engine_build.rs calls store_morph_source at 2 production sites and reads `self.morph_source` directly at 2 more, so the getter is test-only and the allow comment is stale.
findings.proposal: Split Engine state into owned sub-structs (registries, per-build ledgers, test instrumentation, caches), each with its own module and reset/accessor methods, so that satellites take the sub-struct they need rather than reaching into `self`.
findings.next_change: Adding a piece of Engine state, such as a new per-build ledger or registry, means editing the struct in lib.rs, the struct literal in engine_admin::with_prelude_and_kernels, the surface reset in engine_build.rs, an accessor in engine_admin, and every satellite that reads it. The agent has to find all of these by grepping 19 files. A missed reset is caught only where a test drives consecutive surfaces, as engine_build's relate_static_facts test does.

findings.statement: The `ShellExtractionResult` Value produced by shell_extract_compute.rs::shell_extraction_result_to_value is decoded by two independent hand-written parsers. One is engine_admin.rs::parse_shell_extraction_result, the highest-CCN function in that file. The other is shell_extract_compute.rs::value_to_shell_extraction_result. They disagree in detail: the engine_admin parser requires the nested type_name strings "MidSurfaceMesh" and "SegmentationResult", which the other parser does not check, and it decodes triangles to usize where the other uses u32. Engine::shell_gui_mesh_data selects compute nodes by the string targets "shell-extract::extract" and "solver::elastic_static", and returns an empty Vec on any decode miss with no diagnostic. Its `// G-allow: library API; production consumer is the pending shell-extract GUI bridge` is false: gui/src-tauri/src/engine.rs calls it at 2 sites.
findings.proposal: Have shell_gui_mesh_data consume the typed value_to_shell_extraction_result, move it next to that function as a free function over (&Snapshot, &CacheStore), and drop the stale G-allow.
findings.next_change: Someone changes the ShellExtractionResult encoding, for example renaming `mid_surface` or adding a through-thickness channel. They must know that a second decoder in engine_admin.rs feeds the GUI. If they miss it, the GUI silently loses its shell overlay, because the decoder returns None. Only harness_topology_selector/shell_extract_gui_accessor.rs would notice, and only for a total break.

findings.statement: deps.rs derives the question 'what does node X read' with three independent graph walks. ReverseDependencyIndex::build_from_graph_and_fields and build_trace_map_and_fields each loop over value cells, constraints, realizations, resolutions, fields and geometry links. They must agree but are built separately at every call site. They already differ: Compute nodes are registered as reverse dependents but get no trace-map entry. The third walk, DependencyMap::from_graph (used by Engine::trace_undef_causes and the dead cache::dirty_set), has different semantics again. It includes Auto cells' default_expr, which the other two skip; it ignores constraints, realizations and fields; and it dedups and sorts reads, while extract_dependency_trace keeps duplicates. #5385 factored geometry_cell_realization_links out so both main walks share it, but agreement is still pinned per edge class by tests named *_both_directions.
findings.proposal: Build the reverse index by inverting the forward trace map, so there is one walk, and point the undef tracer at the trace map instead of DependencyMap.
findings.next_change: Adding a new read-edge kind (a new node kind, or a let reading a realization through a new query form) means editing both main walks and remembering DependencyMap. If DependencyMap is missed, undef-cause tracing omits the new edge with no failure. If only one main walk is edited, the dirty cone and the per-node trace disagree, which surfaces as stale values in an edit test only when one exists for that edge kind.

findings.statement: The name units.rs misdescribes its contents. Of its 1,910 production lines, lines 1-1,690 (88%) are the compiler's builtin catalogue: 16 name tables (GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES, GEOMETRY_TOPOLOGY_SELECTOR_NAMES, FIELD_OP_NAMES, DATUM_CONSTRUCTOR_NAMES and others), 15 is_* predicates and their *_result_type functions, and selector-composition type checking. Only about 220 lines (UnitRegistry, UnitEntry, UnitResolveError, resolve_unit_expr, unit_to_scalar) concern units. The file opens with `use super::*;`, and lib.rs re-exports it back with `pub(crate) use units::*;`, so its items are visible unqualified in every module of the crate. This is one instance of a crate-wide flat namespace: reify-compiler's lib.rs has 28 `pub(crate) use <mod>::*` globs, and 27 of its 56 top-level source files start with `use super::*;`.
findings.proposal: Move the builtin tables into builtin_families.rs, or straight into reify-builtins rows per docs/prds/v0_6/builtin-signature-registry.md, leaving units.rs with units only. Replace the lib.rs glob re-exports with explicit `use crate::<mod>::{..}` imports.
findings.next_change: Someone adding a builtin family or selector looks in geometry.rs, builtin_signatures.rs or builtin_registry.rs and does not expect the tables to live in units.rs. Because of the glob namespace, a function defined in any of the 27 glob-importing modules can be called unqualified anywhere in the crate, so a call site gives no hint where the definition lives. A name clash between two glob exports surfaces only as an ambiguity error at a use site.

findings.statement: Each builtin's facts are restated in parallel string-keyed tables, and overlaps between them are resolved by the order of an if-ladder. units.rs's 16 tables hold 177 entries but only 166 distinct names, so 11 names appear in two tables. `union` and `difference` are in both GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES and SELECTOR_COMPOSITION_NAMES. `affine_apply` is in both GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES and AFFINE_ALGEBRA_NAMES. Which family claims a name depends on where its arm sits in expr.rs's result-type ladder of about 30 arms, an ordering described in prose and pinned by tests (affine_algebra_names_never_reach_the_terminal_fallback). Per-position facts are restated too: builtin_arg_slots states index, name and dimension; its own comment says the arg names are 'COPIED from geometry.rs's lowering sites'; reify-ir arg_acceptance.rs restates the dimension at eval time; unresolved_function.rs holds a union oracle plus hand-copied signature strings. builtin_arg_slots itself is a 762-line match with 28 arms, of which 537 lines (70.5%) are comments. Much of that prose is task history and reviewer-answering text ('the FOURTH builtin…', 'MEASURED PREFIX DIVERGENCE'), and the module header declares those arms authoritative. reify-builtins (#6001) is the intended single home but has seeded only the parse and analysis families, and is_known_builtin consults both regimes.
findings.proposal: Continue the builtin-signature-registry migration so each builtin is one row carrying arity, arg slots and result. Move per-arm rationale into the row's `basis` field or the PRD, and leave a pointer in the code.
findings.next_change: Adding a geometry builtin with a LENGTH or ANGLE argument today means editing GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES (and a result-type arm if needed), a builtin_arg_slots arm whose arg names must match geometry.rs's lowering, arg_acceptance.rs, and possibly the ladder order in expr.rs, after first choosing between the legacy tables and reify-builtins rows. The units_length_closure_guard test catches a missed LENGTH or ANGLE position. Nothing catches a ladder-order shadowing beyond the per-name tests, or arg-name drift between geometry.rs and the slot table.

findings.statement: reify-eval's integration tests drive the engine through cfg(test-instrumentation) seams that expose its private state. Engine::cache_store_mut hands tests `&mut CacheStore`, and they `put` NodeCache entries directly. cache_store, warm_pool_mut and about a dozen last_* counters are read the same way. Engine::cell_eval_ctx is kept alive only for a parity test, via `#[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code))]` with a comment saying its last production caller was removed. The morph_source getter is used only by morph_producer.rs tests, while production reads the field directly. Each of these seams fixes the shape of NodeCache, CacheStore and the Engine counters in place, so the redesign the prior cache.rs finding proposes (diagnostics as a required NodeCache argument) would also require editing every test that seeds the cache.
findings.proposal: Give tests behavioural seams (edit/eval drivers, fixtures that produce a given cache state through eval) and narrow or remove cache_store_mut. Delete Engine::cell_eval_ctx and the test-only morph_source getter.
findings.next_change: A change to NodeCache construction, such as making diagnostics or freshness a required argument, or to CacheStore's dirty bookkeeping, must also update 65 direct cache-seeding sites in 18 integration-test files. Those tests check the cache layout rather than engine behaviour, so a behaviour-preserving refactor turns them red while a behaviour-changing one can stay green.

findings.statement: cache.rs keeps public peers of the live invalidation path that production never calls. `pub fn dirty_set` has no caller anywhere, takes unused `_graph` and `_values` parameters, and its doc claims it is 're-evaluating and checking for early cutoff', which it does not do. check_early_cutoff and compute_input_hash are called only from cache.rs's own tests. The free function derive_output_freshness has no production caller. DependencyMap::topological_order is called only by dirty_set. Meanwhile two live dirty mechanisms coexist: the one-hop CacheStore.dirty_reasons (invalidate_dependents in engine_edit.rs; is_dirty, clear_dirty and clear_dependents_dirty in eval_cached) and the transitive dirty::compute_dirty_cone (5 production sites in engine_edit.rs). The unwired freshness walk is a third (prior finding).
findings.proposal: Delete dirty_set, check_early_cutoff, compute_input_hash and DependencyMap::topological_order along with their unit tests, and keep the derive_output_freshness truth table only behind the _with_cause variant that production uses.
findings.next_change: Someone changing early-cutoff or dirty-propagation semantics, for example how NaN or diagnostics affect cutoff, finds check_early_cutoff and dirty_set by name and may edit them instead of record_evaluation_with_freshness and dirty::compute_dirty_cone. Their unit tests stay green either way, so the wrong edit is caught only if an engine-level incremental test happens to cover the semantic.

findings.statement: The curvature Surface→Matrix<2,2> overload decides 'face selector' by matching the inner call's function name against FACE_PRODUCING_SELECTOR_NAMES (faces, faces_by_area, faces_by_normal, adjacent_faces). It does not read the selector's type, even though since task 4118 topology_selector_result_type types 11 selectors as Type::Selector(SelectorKind::Face), and the ResolveSelector node the detector unwraps carries that type. geometry_query_arg_aware_result_type's doc still says topology_selector_result_type 'returns Type::List(Geometry) for BOTH faces() and edges()', which is no longer true. So curvature over an indexed face_perpendicular_to, mid_surface, extremal_by_bbox or similar face selector degrades to Scalar<Curvature> while the same expression over faces(...) gets the Matrix type.
findings.proposal: Classify by `selector.result_type == Type::Selector(SelectorKind::Face)` on the ResolveSelector arm, keep a name check only for the still-List adjacent_faces, and correct the doc.
findings.next_change: Someone adds a face selector, or asks why curvature(extremal_by_bbox(b)[0]) is a scalar. They have to find a second, name-keyed list that the selector's type already makes redundant. The doc tells them the type system cannot tell faces from edges, which points them away from the type-based fix. Only the per-name subset test guards the list.

findings.statement: CompiledExpr content-hash domain tags are hand-picked `pub const TAG_*: u8` values. The allocation policy exists only in prose, and the prose contradicts itself. The header says bytes 20-23 are reserved for CachedResult::content_hash in reify-eval/src/cache.rs, which uses the bare literals [20], [21], [22] and [23] rather than named constants. Yet TAG_STRUCTURE_INSTANCE_CTOR = 20 carries the comment 'Tags 20–23 were free'. No test or const assertion checks that the 26 TAG constants are distinct. If two expression kinds shared a tag, structurally different expressions with equal sub-hashes would collide, and early cutoff would treat a changed expression as Unchanged.
findings.proposal: Add a const-evaluated uniqueness assertion over the TAG_* array, name the CachedResult tags in cache.rs, and replace the reservation prose with that assertion.
findings.next_change: The next CompiledExpr variant needs a tag. The agent must read and reconcile two contradictory comments to pick the next byte (the header says 29). A mistaken reuse compiles, passes the walker exhaustiveness checks, and shows up only as an incremental-eval staleness bug.

findings.verdict_notes: Read reify-ir/src/expr.rs 450-495 and the tag tests (2335-2420, 2205-2240); read cache.rs 190-215; git grep for any tag-distinctness assertion — There are 26 pub const TAG_*: u8. The header reserves 20-23 for CachedResult, yet TAG_STRUCTURE_INSTANCE_CTOR = 20 with the comment 'Tags 20-23 were free'. cache.rs uses bare ContentHash::of(&[20..23]). The existing test locks only individual values (a subset) and the match-collision regression test; none asserts that all TAG_* values are mutually distinct. The header says to use 29 next. The collision risk is real but sits in a separately domain-separated CachedResult hash, so the practical risk is lower than the framing suggests.

findings.statement:
`Engine` is defined at reify-eval's crate root with 67 fields (2 of them cfg-gated). Because it sits at the root, every child module can read its private fields. 15 files do so directly via `self.<field>` in production code: engine_admin 50 fields, engine_eval 35, engine_build 24, engine_edit 23, engine_constraints 15, engine_purposes 10, engine_compute 9, and 8 more. There are 23 `impl Engine` blocks across 18 files.

The struct mixes about 6 independent lifetime classes:
- configuration (build_scheduler, mesh_contract_mode, max_unfold_*)
- per-build side tables (topology_attribute_table, swept_kind_table, realization_handles, achieved_repr_tol, relate_static_facts)
- per-eval artifacts (functions, meta_map, objectives, compiled_fields)
- purpose state (5 maps)
- cross-edit caches (cache, warm_pool, realization_cache)
- test instrumentation (9 `last_*`/counter fields)

Each field's class is recorded twice. It appears in its lib.rs doc comment (8 doc mentions of `reset_per_build_state`). It also appears in `engine_build.rs::reset_per_build_state`'s exhaustive destructure, which groups fields under reset-every / reset-on-build / reset-on-tessellate / MUST-SURVIVE headings. The destructure turns a forgotten classification into a compile error, but not a wrong one. That function's own comment records such a misclassification: relate_static_facts was cleared on every surface, a 'silent WIPE' (#5415).
findings.proposal: Group the fields into owned sub-structs by lifetime class, for example `EngineConfig`, `PerBuildState` (with a `reset(surface)` method), `EvalArtifacts`, `PurposeState`, `Caches` and `Instrumentation`. Satellite files then borrow the sub-struct they need, and the reset becomes the sub-struct's own method. A new field's class is chosen by where it is declared, not by a comment plus a separate destructure.

findings.statement:
The content-hash identity of a value-cell node is `ContentHash::of_str(&format!("{}", id)).combine(default_expr.map(content_hash).unwrap_or(ContentHash(0)))`. It is written out inline at 6 sites in `EvaluationGraph::from_templates`: top-level cells, collection elements, keyed members, plain subs, guard members, and else members. It is written again at 2 sites in engine_edit.rs, the collection-count re-elaboration (and its second copy). `ValueCellNode` has only public fields and no constructor. `ConstraintNodeData` is likewise built literally 4 times in graph.rs and twice in engine_edit.rs.

The cold path (from_templates) and the edit path (engine_edit re-elaboration) must produce byte-identical hashes for the same cell, or incremental cache keys diverge from cold ones (the INV-EVAL-4 class). Nothing links the two except copy discipline. structural_classifier.rs restates the formula in a doc comment and reasons about what it excludes.

`from_templates` itself is one 424-line function (322 code lines) nested 13 indents deep. It also scans the count-literal of collection subs by hand, through nested `if let` on `CompiledExprKind::Literal` and `ValueRef`.
findings.proposal: Add `ValueCellNode::new(id, kind, cell_type, default_expr)` and `ConstraintNodeData::from_compiled(&CompiledConstraint)` (with a scoped-id variant). Have them compute `content_hash`, and keep the hash field writable only through those constructors. Split from_templates per declaration kind, so that each arm calls the constructor.
findings.next_change: Plausible change: change what a value cell's identity covers, for example adding `kind` so that the role flip structural_classifier documents becomes hash-visible, or hashing `cell_type`. The agent must find all 8 inline sites in two files. Missing an engine_edit site makes a collection that grew at edit time hash differently from a cold eval of the same source, which shows up as spurious cache misses or stale hits. Only behavioural cache tests would notice, and nothing pins node equality across the two paths.

findings.statement:
Active-purpose state is spread across 5 parallel `HashMap`s on Engine, all keyed by the purpose-name string:
- active_purposes
- active_purpose_bindings
- active_objective_map
- active_purpose_let_cells
- active_tolerance_scope (derived)

compiled_purposes holds the definitions, looked up by linear name scan. The field docs say these are 'populated/cleared in lockstep', but the lockstep is kept by hand. The insert half is in `activate_purpose_constraints_with_bindings_inner` (a 272-line method), the remove half in `deactivate_purpose`, and two re-injection blocks in engine_eval.rs (around L5226 and L9570) clear active_purposes, active_objective_map and active_tolerance_scope. Neither of those blocks clears active_purpose_let_cells.

Activation is temporally coupled. The `_inner` call returns `bool`, and every caller must then call `rebuild_purpose_infrastructure()`; 4 caller pairs do this by hand. `deactivate_purpose` re-inlines the same rebuild (reverse_index, trace_map, rebuild_cone, then recompute_tolerance_scope) instead of calling it.

The docs on `activate_purpose` still describe task γ as pending ('Until task γ lands…'), but `activate_purpose_with_bindings` is the γ API and exists in the same file.
findings.proposal: Replace the maps with one `HashMap<PurposeName, ActivePurpose { constraints, bindings, objective, let_cells }>` owned by a `PurposeState` type. Its `activate`, `deactivate` and `reinject_all(&mut EvalState)` methods include the infrastructure rebuild, and active_tolerance_scope is derived from it on demand.
findings.next_change: Plausible change: add a fifth piece of per-purpose state (for example injected realizations or demand overrides), or a new re-activation site (a third surface that rebuilds the snapshot). The agent must find every place the parallel maps are inserted, removed, cleared or re-injected, across engine_purposes.rs and engine_eval.rs, and remember to pair the activation with a rebuild. The current omission shows the failure mode: active_purpose_let_cells keeps entries across a re-eval in which a purpose vanished from compiled_purposes, and deactivate_purpose can never remove them, because its early return keys on active_purposes. Nothing catches this; no test inspects the maps' agreement.

findings.statement:
Instance paths are meaningful strings. `ValueCellId.entity` is a `String`. It is built by `format!("{}.{}[{}]", …)` at 13 sites in the compiler and eval, and by `MemberKey::path_segment` for keyed members, which writes `sub[<Debug-quoted key>]`.

It is then parsed ad hoc in at least 9 places in reify-eval production code:
- `strip_prefix` (engine_eval ×2, unfold)
- `starts_with` (unfold, tolerance_scope)
- `rsplit_once('.')` / `rsplit('.')` taking 'the last segment is the sub name' (geometry_ops, relate_solve)
- resolve_order's `strip_collection_indices`, which removes `[…]` with a character-level depth scanner

Two incompatible scopings coexist: structure-name-scoped template cells and instance-path-scoped cells. `normalize_cell_id` bridges them at every hop of the transitive walk. `build_instance_path_structure_map` re-walks the sub-component tree, 'mirroring structural_query.rs' (cited by line numbers), so that the bridge has a lookup table.

The `rsplit('.')` parsers cannot represent the grammar `path_segment` produces: a key containing '.' (for example `vents["a.b"]`) splits inside the quotes.
findings.proposal: Introduce a typed `InstancePath(Vec<PathSegment { sub: Name, index: Option<Index | Key> }>)` built at elaboration time. Have `ValueCellId` carry it, or a cheap interned handle to it, with Display used only at boundaries. Provide `structure_scope()` and `owning_sub()` as methods, replacing normalize_cell_id, strip_collection_indices and the rsplit parsers.
findings.next_change: Plausible change: add a new sub-collection addressing form, or a new consumer that needs the 'owning sub' of a cell (for example cross-sub relates over keyed members). The agent must know the path grammar, which is defined only by the 13 format sites and path_segment, and must check every parser. A wrong version compiles and only misbehaves on unusual keys or nesting. Nothing centralises the grammar, and no test fuzzes the parsers against path_segment output.

findings.statement:
Each geometric relation's facts are spread across parallel string-keyed tables in relation_signatures.rs:
- `RELATION_FN_NAMES`
- `is_relation_shared_verb`
- `relation_fn_result_type`
- `relation_delta_dof`
- `relation_delta_dof_kinds`
- `relation_metric_slot`
- `relation_operand_datum`
- `check_relation_arg_types` (`name == "tangent"`, `name == "distance"`)

The 'only the arity-3 form is a relation' policy for angle, distance and offset is encoded as 10 separate `args.len() == 3` guards. Agreement is kept by comment: '…so all four offset arms agree'. offset's arity-2 form is resolved in yet another file (units.rs `datum_constructor_result_type`).

The test that pins rot+trans == ΔDOF iterates a third hand-written list (`curated`), not RELATION_FN_NAMES. The constant's own doc says '**9 names**', but it holds 10 (fasten was added).
findings.proposal: Use one `RelationSig` descriptor per relation: `{name, arity: Arity, operands: OperandPolicy, metric_slot, codim: Codim}`, where Codim is `Fixed{rot,trans}`, `ByDatum(fn)` or `Tangent`. Keep them in a single static table that every resolver reads. Tests then iterate the table, so adding a relation is one row.
findings.next_change: Plausible change: add a relation (for example `symmetric` or `coaxial`), or give an existing one an arity overload as offset received. The agent must edit 6-7 tables plus units.rs and the two test lists. If it omits the entry in `relation_delta_dof_kinds`, the result is `None`, which joint_self_check treats as gradual (skip). Omitting `relation_operand_datum` leaves operands unpoliced. Neither omission is caught: the sum test only covers shapes listed in `curated`.

findings.statement:
Production engines still do not declare their compute-registration posture. It is inferred: `engine_compute.rs::soft_no_trampoline_diagnostic` emits a Warning when `compute_registry.fns.is_empty()` and an Error otherwise. An engine nobody registered is therefore indistinguishable from a deliberate opt-out.

The registration lint (`scripts/check-compute-trampoline-registration.sh`) checks only a literal table of 3 known sites: CLI main.rs, GUI engine.rs and test_runner.rs. The CLI MCP server's `ensure_engine` is a fourth production engine-construction site. It builds `Engine::new(SimpleConstraintChecker, None)`, registers nothing, and has no test pinning that posture. Its comment says it wires `set_persistent_cache_dir` so that 'MCP/GUI eval sessions also hit and populate the persistent on-disk cache'. The persistent lookup sits inside `run_compute_dispatch`, which a trampoline-less engine's eval path never reaches through `OptimizedComputeDispatcher::from_registry`.

docs/invariants.md INV-FEA-1 still names `Engine::new_production` as the mechanism, status 'proposed'; no such constructor exists.
findings.proposal: Make the posture a required constructor argument or type, for example `Engine::new(checker, kernel, Registration::Production(morph) | Registration::None { reason })`. The severity decision then reads the declared posture instead of `fns.is_empty()`. Put the MCP context's choice, and its persistent-cache comment, under a locking test.
findings.next_change: Plausible change: add or modify an entry point (a new MCP tool, a batch runner, a daemon) that constructs an Engine. The agent copies `Engine::new(...)` and gets the 'deliberate opt-out' Warning posture by default, so FEA constraints evaluate Indeterminate. The lint does not see the new site, and nothing forces the author to decide.

findings.statement:
Engine exposes 28 `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-instrumentation"))]` public methods. They include raw mutable access to internals: `cache_store_mut`, `snapshot_mut`, `warm_pool_mut`, `realization_cache`, `set_build_scheduler`, `set_achieved_repr_tol_for_test` and `with_test_kernels_and_registry`. reify-eval enables the feature on itself through a self-dev-dependency, as do reify-lsp and reify-eval-fea-tests.

The production struct also carries 9 always-present counters whose only purpose is letting tests observe internal control flow: `last_guard_phase_group_evals`, `last_role_flip_probes`, `last_param_override_*` ×2, `last_sub_component_unknown_structure_errors`, `last_dispatch_count`, `geometry_revalidation_slow_path`, `last_diff_value_cells` (marked `#[allow(dead_code)]`), and `morph_source` (also marked `#[allow(dead_code)]`). It carries 2 more cfg-gated test-only fields: `test_registry_override` and `panic_on_eval_cells`. Tests reach in heavily: `cache_store_mut()` is called 121 times across 24 files.
findings.proposal: Replace the mutators with behaviour-level seams: fixture constructors that build an Engine in a given cache state through public eval calls, and a single read-only `EngineProbe` snapshot of counters returned by value. Retire the always-present counters that only tests read, or fold them into the journal (EventJournal already records evaluation events).
findings.next_change: Plausible change: refactor the eval cache's internal shape, or move it out of Engine (see finding .1). 24 test files that mutate `CacheStore` directly through `cache_store_mut` must be rewritten, even though the observable behaviour (values, diagnostics, dispatch counts) is unchanged. Conversely, a behaviour regression can hide behind a test that pokes the cache into the expected state. Reviewers cannot tell which of the 121 call sites are setup and which assert on internals.

findings.statement:
Nine geometry-kind enums in types.rs each carry a hand-maintained private `const ALL: [Self; N]` and a `pub const VARIANT_COUNT = Self::ALL.len()`. The enums are PrimitiveKind, BooleanOp, ModifyKind, TransformKind, PatternKind, SweepKind, CurveKind, ProfileKind and SurfaceKind. Each also carries a copy of the same ~10-line 'Maintenance contract' doc paragraph, which says ALL is 'the single source of truth' and 'cannot independently drift'.

Nothing ties ALL to the enum. Adding a variant compiles with ALL and VARIANT_COUNT unchanged; only the exhaustive Display match forces an edit. The downstream registry-completeness locks (`geometry_modify` CASES assert, reify-eval `compile_geometry_op_registry_completeness`, `compile_geometry_op_characterization`) compare against the stale count and pass. So the tripwire fails in exactly the case it exists for.

reify-compiler already depends on strum, and reify-core already derives `strum::EnumCount` for TypeDiscriminants.
findings.proposal: Derive `strum::EnumCount` (and `EnumIter` where iteration is needed) on the 9 enums. Delete the ALL arrays and the 9 copied paragraphs, so VARIANT_COUNT is the compiler-derived `COUNT`.
findings.next_change: Plausible change: add a geometry primitive or kind (for example `PrimitiveKind::Ellipsoid`). Following the doc, the agent extends Display, which the compiler forces, and believes the VARIANT_COUNT locks will force the registry rows. If the agent forgets ALL, they don't fire, so the new kind can ship without a compile-registry row or characterization case.

The ALL arrays do not tie to the enum, since an added variant still compiles with ALL and VARIANT_COUNT unchanged. The registry completeness lock compares a separate hand-written ALL_PRIMITIVE against VARIANT_COUNT, so both stay stale together. strum is available in reify-compiler. Weakened: the scenario that a new kind can ship without a registry row or characterization case is not shown. I did not check whether the compile/dispatch code matches exhaustively on the kind enums, in which case the compiler would force the row.

findings.statement:
lib.rs is 48% comments, and the Engine struct alone is 699 comment lines out of 770. Those comments hold task history, the names of tests that pin behaviour, and file:line pointers, all of which have drifted at this tree:
- `realization_cache.rs:101-116` now points at the `ConversionSlot` enum; `lookup` is at :307.
- `types.rs:854-857` now points at `find_template`.
- `tests/tolerance_wiring_e2e.rs` has moved to `tests/harness_tolerance/`.
- The mod comments on `cell_commit` and `detectors` say 'no external callers yet', but cell_commit is called from 4 files and detectors from 2.
- `morph_source`'s doc says its consumer 'lands in #4744 step-16' and keeps `#[allow(dead_code)]`, but engine_build.rs now calls it twice.

The file also carries a re-export shim chain kept 'so the crate-root paths … keep resolving unchanged': 6 reify_compute_contract types, `pub(crate) use reify_ir::arg_acceptance`, and `graph::CancellationHandle`, which graph.rs itself re-exports from reify_compute_contract.
findings.proposal: Move each field's rationale into the PRD the field's task cites (most already have one), and keep a one-line purpose per field. Delete the line-number pointers in favour of symbol names. Retire the compat re-exports by migrating downstream imports to reify_compute_contract.
findings.next_change: Plausible change: any engine change starts by reading the Engine struct to learn a field's contract. The agent spends about 700 lines of context and follows pointers that now land on unrelated code. It may trust 'no production caller yet', or 'no external callers', and skip a site that does use the field. Nothing checks prose.

findings.statement:
`query_kind` on `ResolvedSchemaQuery` and on `CompiledExprKind::PurposeReflectiveAggregation` is a `String` carrying an enum: 'params', 'geometric_params' or 'material_params'. It is defined as a string slice at compiler expr.rs:1078, and spelled again in traits.rs, reify-ir expr.rs and 5 times in engine_purposes.rs.

When no resolved query matches, the runtime fallback string-compares the kind. An unknown kind returns an empty member list, which produces a vacuous-true `forall`, so the purpose constraint silently passes.
findings.proposal: Parse the kind into an enum `ReflectiveQueryKind { Params, GeometricParams, MaterialParams }` at the compiler boundary, and carry the enum in IR. The fallback then becomes an exhaustive `match` with the per-kind predicate.
findings.next_change: Plausible change: add a reflective query kind (for example kinematic_params). The agent adds it to the compiler slice and to traits.rs, but not to engine_purposes' fallback arm. When a query is unresolved (the wildcard-subject case), constraints over the new kind evaluate vacuously true. It compiles, and no exhaustiveness check catches it.

findings.statement:
The ValueCell BFS body, including the edge-#12 Compute→output-cell expansion, is written twice: in `compute_dirty_cone` and again inside `compute_dirty_cone_with_realizations`. The second copy differs by one extra realization re-seed. Only the realization-frontier loop dispatches on `NodeId` with an exhaustive `match`; both ValueCell loops use `if let` chains, so a new `NodeId` variant is silently treated as a leaf there.

The two functions also have different transitive closure. The plain one does not walk through realizations, and the doc of the other states 'every arm rounds toward INCLUSION'. Yet `compute_dirty_cone_with_realizations` has exactly one production caller, which passes an empty ValueCell seed set (engine_edit.rs:685), so its name describes an input it is never given.
findings.proposal: Use one walker, `dirty_cone(seeds: Seeds { cells, realizations }, policy)`, with a single exhaustive `match` on `NodeId` per frontier, and name it for what the edit path actually seeds.
findings.next_change: Plausible change: add a dependency edge kind or a NodeId variant (for example an analysis node consuming compute outputs). The agent updates the exhaustive realization match because the compiler forces it, but misses the two `if let` ValueCell loops. Edit-time dirty cones then omit the new node's dependents, which means stale results after an edit. Only an end-to-end edit test on the new node kind would catch it.

findings.statement: The datum-projection table ('receiver kind x member -> codomain') has three independent homes with no derivation or parity check between them: the compiler typing table plus DATUM_PROJECTION_MEMBERS in datum_projection.rs (whose doc calls it 'the single source of truth'), reify-expr's eval_datum_projection, and reify-eval geometry_ops.rs's SELF_DATUM_PROJECTION_MEMBERS (described only in prose as 'LOCKSTEP'). They have already drifted. The compiler types Frame(_).yz_plane and .zx_plane as Plane, but eval_datum_projection's Value::Frame arm has no arm for either, so they evaluate to Undef with no diagnostic. Task #6100 (pending) tracks that one instance. The three-table structure stays after it is fixed.

Until then, add a parity test that iterates DATUM_PROJECTION_MEMBERS x {Axis, Plane, Frame, Direction, StructureRef} and asserts that every Resolved pair evaluates to a non-Undef value of the declared kind.
findings.next_change: Geometric-relations γ/η work 'extends this table here' (the module doc says so). Nothing catches a wrong version: the compiler-side unit tests pass, the expression type-checks, and eval silently yields Undef.

findings.statement: reify-compiler's crate root flattens the contents of 29 modules (325 top-level pub/pub(crate) items) via `pub(crate) use X::*` / `pub use types::*`, and 27 source files import that root wholesale with a top-level `use super::*;`. Eight of them are in this slice: coerce, datum_projection, diagnostics, geometry_boolean, geometry_curve, geometry_transform, ice and termination. termination.rs's only import is `use super::*`. It names TopologyTemplate, GuardState, CompiledExpr, ValueCellId, Diagnostic, DiagnosticLabel, HashMap and HashSet, and the file says where none of them come from. Its three helpers are pub(crate) and globbed into the root, although only check_recursive_termination has an external caller (post_passes.rs, by path).
findings.proposal: Replace each top-level `use super::*` with explicit imports (mechanical with rust-analyzer), shrink the root globs to the named items other modules actually use, and ratchet the count of top-level `use super::*`.
findings.next_change: An agent moves or renames a function in one of these files, or adds a dependency between two peers. It must resolve names through a 325-item glob union. Ambiguity surfaces only when two globs collide, and any file can silently start depending on any peer, so peer cycles stay invisible. rustc catches outright breakage. Nothing catches a growing tangle or a reader's wrong guess about where a name lives.

findings.statement: joint_self_check.rs is a shallow module that exports the pieces of the §7.1 DOF self-check law but not the law itself. It exposes five pub(crate) functions (residual_kinds, body_has_undecidable_kind_split, dof_kind_of, declared_kinds, check_joint_dof). The gate that makes the verdict sound (skip on a Type::Error DOF; emit E_ARG_TYPE_MISMATCH and skip on an unclassifiable DOF; skip on an undecidable rot/trans split; only then compare residual against declared) is reimplemented in compile_builder/entities_phase.rs. The module's own docs assign that duty to 'the caller' in two places. Its tests drive each piece separately, so nothing tests the composed law.
findings.proposal: Expose one entry point, e.g. joint_dof_diagnostics(joint_name, declared fields [(name, Type, span)], body, span) -> Vec<Diagnostic>, that owns both gradualism gates and the verdict. Make the pieces private and drive tests through that seam.
findings.next_change: An agent adds a DOF kind (e.g. Orientation(2) when SO(2) lands) or a relation whose count is curated but whose kind split is not (like tangent). It edits joint_self_check.rs, but must also know that the verdict gating lives in entities_phase.rs. A second caller, or a refactor that calls check_joint_dof without the gates, emits a spurious E_JOINT_DOF_MISMATCH. The module's piecewise unit tests cannot catch that.

findings.statement: The compiler routes geometry ops on raw name strings that are respelled at every hop. geometry.rs's router matches a literal name group and calls a satellite. The satellite (compile_boolean_op / compile_curve_op / compile_transform_op / compile_modify_op) re-matches the same names and ends in `_ => unreachable!()`. compile_boolean_op then matches the names a third time to pick a BooleanOp. Meanwhile reify-ir already has an OpDescriptor table that maps names (e.g. ["union","union_all"]) to GeometryOpDiscriminants, and compile dispatch never consults it.
findings.proposal: Parse the name to GeometryOpDiscriminants once through the OpDescriptor table at the router and dispatch on the enum with an exhaustive match, so a missing arm is a compile error rather than a runtime unreachable! (the τ9 #6011 bridge covers the name-set half).
findings.next_change: An agent adds an op or an alias (e.g. 'subtract' for difference). It edits the router group, the satellite match, the inner op map, GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES, the OpDescriptor names and geometry_traits_inference. If it misses a satellite arm, the compiler panics at unreachable! on user input. That is caught only if some test compiles that exact name.

findings.statement: Engine exposes two mirrored pass-through method sets over DemandRegistry, one for the production registry (engine_demand.rs) and one for the observed registry (observed_demand.rs). The incremental mutators add_demand and remove_demand are public with no production caller. They are temporally coupled: the caller must call rebuild_demand_cone afterwards, and they skip the mark_demand_pruned_pending prune-safety step that set_demand_selective performs. Several inspection methods exist only for tests.
findings.proposal: Collapse the production mutation surface to set_demand_selective (or a single toggle that rebuilds and marks atomically), make add/remove private or delete them, and expose one read-only demand view for tests instead of per-field inspection methods.
findings.next_change: A GUI change toggles one body's visibility incrementally and reaches for add_demand/remove_demand, the obvious incremental API. Unless it also calls rebuild_demand_cone and mark_demand_pruned_pending in that order, the hidden body's cached Final values are served stale until the next warm build re-marks them. No test exercises that sequence.

findings.statement:
`Finding` has no structured kind or location. Every multi-kind detector puts its kind into `summary` as a `<kind>: ` prefix (the 'PTODO kind-as-prefix convention' that lib.rs, pdoccover, pdcheck and pcite each cite), and most also embed `line N:` in that text. That string is parsed back by:
- `ptodo::fingerprint`, the key of the merge-gate ptodo-baseline.txt ratchet: `split_once(':')` plus a hand parser that strips `line <digits>: `.
- `ptodo::is_g_allow_finding`: `starts_with("g-allow-")`.
- `ptodo::g_allow_finding_line`: `split_once(": line ")`. It sits behind a `debug_assert`, so a release build silently sorts at line 0.
- the /audit skill's routing templates, which tell the agent to take `<kind>` and `<n>` from `finding.summary`.
- test helpers.
`EvidenceRef::FileLine` was added so consumers would 'read it rather than parsing it out of the summary', but only PCITE emits it. `Finding.task_id` is a name that lies: structural detectors store a file path in it. Inside PTODO it holds a path for the structural and liveness kinds and a numeric task id for the inverse kinds, while `fingerprint`'s doc says it is a path 'for all PTODO kinds'.
findings.proposal: Give Finding a typed `kind` (a per-pattern enum serialised as today's token) and require `EvidenceRef::FileLine` for located findings. Derive `fingerprint` and the sort keys from those fields, and render `summary` from them for humans only. Replace `task_id` with a `subject` enum (Task(id) | Path(path)) so the field says which it holds.
findings.next_change:
Add a PTODO kind, reword a summary (adding a colon to the text or moving the `line N:` clause), or start reporting lines in PDIAG or PDSSENTINEL. To do that safely the agent must know three things that are stated nowhere near `Finding`:
- `ptodo::fingerprint` derives the committed baseline keys from the summary text.
- `g_allow_finding_line` re-parses the line number in order to sort.
- `.claude/skills/audit/references/severity-routing.md` scrapes `<kind>` and `<n>` out of the summary to build follow-up titles.
The only catches are test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh, which reds as a whole-baseline stale storm rather than naming the cause, and summary-substring asserts in tests. Nothing catches the skill-side breakage, and the release-mode line-0 fallback is invisible.

findings.statement:
The question 'is this source line or path test-only or opted out?' has several homes inside one crate, with divergent semantics:
- cfg(test) attribute (4 recognisers):
  - pdiag::is_cfg_test_attr accepts `#[cfg(test)]` and `cfg(any(test,…))`, rejects anything containing `not(`, and explicitly rejects `feature = "test-*"` as production-reachable.
  - p2_consumer_stub::is_test_cfg_attr ACCEPTS `feature = "test…"` and `all(test,…)`.
  - pdoccover::is_cfg_test_attr accepts only exact `#[cfg(test)]` / `#![cfg(test)]`.
  - jcodemunch_client::extract_suppression uses `line.contains("cfg(test)")`.
- test path (2 rules): lib.rs::is_test_path calls itself 'the crate's *single* canonical test-path predicate' (matches `_test.rs`, `.test.`, `__tests__/`). pdiag::is_swept_path gate 4 is a different rule (a `tests` segment, or a `tests`/`*_tests` stem).
- allow(dead_code): ptodo::allow_dead_code_attr scans for a whole `dead_code` token and rejects `dead_codex`. jcodemunch_client::extract_suppression uses a substring `contains("dead_code")`.
- G-allow body grammar (3 copies, 2 semantics): ptodo::g_allow_marker_body, jcodemunch_client::extract_g_allow, and scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh `G_ALLOW_RE.search` (free-floating).
- cfg(test)-region trackers (2, deliberately different): pdiag's brace counting is literal-unaware; pdoccover's blanks literals first.
findings.proposal: Move the Rust source-shape vocabulary into one lower module, next to scan_util: a code view with comment and literal masking, a cfg(test)-region tracker, the attribute recognisers, and the G-allow body grammar. Where a detector genuinely needs a different policy (pdiag's line-granular mask), make the policy a named parameter of that module rather than a private copy. Have lib::is_test_path and pdiag's test-locus gate share one rule or carry distinct names.
findings.next_change: Write a new structural detector (the crate adds roughly one per PRD), or fix a false positive on a `cfg(any(test, feature=…))` or `feature = "test-support"` body in one detector. The agent copies whichever recogniser is nearest. To match crate-wide semantics they would have to find and compare four implementations whose docs each claim to be authoritative. Nothing ties them together, so a fix lands in one detector and the next detector re-discovers the bug, as eae2a341aa did.

findings.statement:
Of GitOps's 12 questions, 9 collapse 'git failed' into an answer (empty Vec, `false`, or `None`) with no fallible variant. Only log_grep, is_gitignored and path_tracked_on have `try_` twins, and the trait doc leaves it to each caller to know when the collapse is unsafe. `ls_files()` is among the collapsed nine, so its 7 consumers each re-decide 'enumeration failed' from emptiness, in four different ways:
- PDOCCOVER: DegenerateInputs, a High `census-empty:` finding.
- PDIAG: `pdiag-census-empty` High, but only when the baseline has rows.
- PTODO: exposes ScanStats.files_scanned for the infra test's floor and otherwise reports clean.
- PDSSENTINEL, PCITE and PPRDSTATUS: silently report clean.
- PDCHECK: reads an empty tracked set as 'every path absent' and stays quiet only because the following `last_commit_for_path` call also fails.
The P5 sweep's High verdict in check_one is likewise built on the infallible `path_tracked_on` and `task_referencing_commits`, whereas the pre-done gate routes the same failures into a Low advisory.
findings.proposal: Add `try_ls_files() -> Result<Vec<String>, String>`, or return a `TrackedFiles` value that cannot be constructed from a failure, and give the remaining collapsed questions try_ forms. Then implement 'degenerate enumeration' once, for example as a crate-level finding emitted by the dispatcher, instead of once per detector.
findings.next_change: A new structural detector calls `ctx.git.ls_files()`. The type does not tell the author that an empty Vec may mean git failed, so whether the new lane fails loud, fails silent or inverts depends on whether the author happens to read PDOCCOVER's DegenerateInputs docs. A lane added to the default sweep that reports clean on a failed enumeration is caught only if someone writes a vacuity test for it.

findings.statement:
Comment lines make up 52-59% of non-blank lines in the production regions of lib.rs, p5_phantom_done.rs, pdiag.rs, pdoccover.rs and ptodo.rs. Much of that prose is reviewer-answering: dated corpus counts, rejected alternatives, 'do not simplify' warnings, and the names of the tests that pin each property. It has drifted from the code. At least nine statements are false at this tree:
- lib.rs Pattern::PTodo says 'all Medium severity' and 'participates … at Medium severity (exit-neutral)', but Kind::severity maps untracked and bare-ignore to High, and orphaned and g-allow-orphaned are High.
- ptodo.rs's module doc says 'all emitting Medium-severity findings'.
- pdiag.rs says 'Unlike PTODO's warn-first Medium lanes'.
- lib.rs's crate doc says 'currently ships three detectors'; there are 13.
- Pattern's naming convention says every variant carries `P<N>` 'so downstream dispatch can route on prefix', but 10 of 18 variants have no digit.
- Severity's doc says Medium 'is reserved for metadata-cleanliness findings'.
- AuditContext's doc says 'the crate never owns a connection or spawns processes itself', but ptodo and pdcheck open tasks.db.
- RealGitOps's doc says 'Untested by the slice-1 integration suite', but tests/real_git_ops.rs has 13 tests.
- pdoccover's section header says 'Pure scanners (stubs — filled in by the TDD steps that follow)'.
findings.proposal: Move measurements, rejected alternatives and test-name pins into the PRDs (the files already cite §-anchors) or into the commit messages that made them. Keep one-line pointers in the code. Let the severity table be derived from code, for example a `Kind::severity` per pattern listed in `--help`, instead of restated in rustdoc.
findings.next_change: An agent adds a PTODO lane or changes a kind's severity, starting from lib.rs's Pattern doc, which is the vocabulary an agent reads first. The doc says PTODO is Medium and exit-neutral, so the agent believes a new High kind would be unusual, or that a Medium change is safe for the exit code. Nothing checks doc claims against `Kind::severity`. Separately, every edit to a detector must wade through and keep consistent prose that is roughly as long as the code, which is how these nine statements went stale.

findings.statement:
Access to the task DB (`tasks_db_path`, which honours the REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB override, and `open_tasks_db`) lives in a peer detector, ptodo. It is not a seam on AuditContext. PDCHECK and the bin import it from ptodo, and PDCHECK opens its own connection inside `check`.
Reporting of DB degradation is a PTODO-specific type (`ptodo::ScanStats` / `ptodo::TasksDbMode`). As a result the bin's `Check::TasksDbBacked` / `Detector::reads_tasks_db()` answers false for PDCHECK, which does read tasks.db and degrades with 'this is NOT a clean bill of health'. `--pattern PDCHECK --require-tasks-db` exits 125 with 'this run set does not include PTODO', so PDCHECK's degradation cannot be guarded.
The canonical-cite grammar, which PPRDSTATUS needs, also lives in ptodo and is imported peer-to-peer (`use crate::ptodo::canonical_cite_occurrences`).
findings.proposal: Move `tasks_db_path` and `open_tasks_db` into task_rows (or onto AuditContext as an optional `tasks_db` handle that the bin opens once). Make DB-lane degradation a crate-level outcome that any detector can return, and let `reads_tasks_db` be derived from it. Move the cite grammar into a lower `cite_grammar` module shared by PTODO and PPRDSTATUS.
findings.next_change: A third lane reads task metadata from tasks.db (the PDCHECK pattern invites it). Or an operator wants `--require-tasks-db` for PDCHECK. The agent must discover that DB access lives in ptodo and that degradation can only be reported through a PTODO type, then either reach into ptodo again or extend `Check` with another variant. A lane that silently skips is caught only by a hand-written stderr assert.

findings.statement:
The exit code carries both the High-finding count (`count.min(254)`) and the infra-error code `ERROR_EXIT = 125`, so a run with exactly 125 High findings exits 125. Both doc comments say otherwise:
- ERROR_EXIT is 'Reserved so it never collides with a High-severity finding count'.
- high_severity_exit_code is 'Capped at 254 (not 255) so that exit code 125 remains unambiguously reserved'. The cap protects 255 (TASKS_DB_ABSENT_EXIT), not 125.
Consumers carry the cost: .claude/skills/audit/references/cli-invocation.md §3.1 has every caller JSON-parse stderr and check `len == 125 && all High` before trusting a 125.
findings.proposal: Make the channel injective: map counts that would land on reserved codes to a neighbour (or saturate at 124), or move infra errors outside 1-254. Fix both comments and pin the boundary with a unit test.
findings.next_change: A dark-factory hook, a new wrapper script or a new detector author branches on the exit code. Trusting the in-code comment, they treat 125 as infra-only and drop a 125-High run as misconfiguration. Knowing to do otherwise requires reading the skill's §3.1 workaround, which lives outside the crate. No test exercises 125 Highs.

findings.proposal: Drive integration tests through `check` and `check_with_stats` over real tempdir fixtures (pdiag's test_support::Fixture already shows the shape). Move pure-grammar tests into in-file `#[cfg(test)]` modules, where private items are visible without `pub`. Delete wrappers such as `resolve_liveness` that exist only for those tests.

findings.statement: No single function owns the user-module front end (read source, derive the module name, parse_with_stdlib, render parse errors, compile with a constraint checker, check the `module` declaration, then evaluate behind the eval guard). Each surface spells it by hand, and the copies differ in substance. The CLI MCP context (load_file, update_source, open_file) compiles with `reify_compiler::compile`. That function's own doc says it uses no prelude and is 'intended only for prelude-module bootstrapping', and that stdlib units such as mm, deg and kg, stdlib traits and stdlib enums are absent and give unresolved-name diagnostics. The same code parses with parse_with_stdlib, and every other surface compiles with compile_with_stdlib_checked plus SimpleConstraintChecker. check_module_path_decl runs only in the CLI (parse_and_compile, and module_dag on the --cfg path). No reify-lsp or mcp_context site calls it. MCP eval also runs without eval_guard::skip_reason, as eval_guard's own doc admits. The three MCP sites have three different parse-error policies: load_file returns Err with rendered messages, update_source returns success:false and changes nothing, and open_file registers the file and clears compiled.
findings.proposal: Give reify_compiler (or a small front-end module that the CLI, LSP, MCP and GUI all depend on) one `compile_user_module(source, path, checker) -> FrontEnd { parsed, compiled, parse_errors }` that includes the module-path check. Put the eval-guard question beside it, so surfaces differ only in what they do with the result. Add one cross-surface test that runs a stdlib-using fixture through each surface and compares error counts.
findings.next_change: Plausible change: add an MCP tool (or a new CLI or LSP surface) that compiles the active file, or change a compile-policy fact such as which checker drives `auto:` feasibility or whether the module-path check runs. The agent copies the nearest sibling site. Doing it right requires knowing that reify_compiler has three compile entry points with different preludes and checkers, that #6798 moved the LSP and CLI onto the real checker, and that the eval guard exists. None of that is visible from mcp_context.rs. Nothing catches a wrong copy: no test compares the diagnostics of one fixture across surfaces, and no MCP test asserts a clean stdlib-using file compiles clean.
