findings.statement: Two structurally disjoint invalidation walks existed: the freshness-unaware dirty cone and propagate_freshness_only, built for async compute completions and never called in production, so an async completion never invalidated dependents; Freshness::default() = Final made an absent cache entry read as authoritative. The briefing lists gating.rs Phase-A hooks as retained dead code awaiting #5023 — verify whether the dead walk was wired, deleted, or is still a retained parity obligation.
findings.checked: Engine::propagate_freshness_only (engine_admin.rs) has zero production callers. Its only callers are tests: tests/harness_cache/freshness_only_production_trigger.rs, harness_geometry/geometry_handle_freshness.rs and harness_topology_selector/topology_selectors_tests.rs. The async completion site in engine_compute.rs calls cache.complete_compute_dispatch_atomically, which writes Freshness::Final with no propagation, and then carries `// TODO(#5023): async completions must invalidate dependents (propagate_freshness_only)`. `impl Default for Freshness` in reify-ir/src/value.rs still returns Final, and CacheStore::freshness still uses unwrap_or_default, so an absent entry still reads as authoritative. gating.rs keeps its G-allow Phase-A hooks. docs/invariants.md INV-EVAL-6 is still 'proposed'. Mechanism today: intent only (TODO plus doc).

findings.statement: Cache-write and diagnostic emission were decoupled by API shape (record_evaluation took no diagnostics; NodeCache held none), so the 2259/2267 fix was convention+tests and a new per-cell-branch diagnostic would silently regress on a cache hit. INV-EVAL-3 proposed diagnostics stored in the cache entry and a shared post-pass detector registry.
findings.checked: Partly mitigated, but the API-shape defect remains. NodeCache.diagnostics exists (task κ #5042). CacheStore::set_node_diagnostics is a post-record setter (μ #5062), and eval_cached replays via Engine::replay_cell_diagnostics at 3 sites. detectors.rs holds a post-pass registry. However, record_evaluation, record_evaluation_with_freshness, record_evaluation_propagating_freshness and commit_cell_result still take no diagnostics. Capture is opt-in: store_cell_replay_diagnostics has 5 production calls against 32 commit_cell_result sites and 13 direct record_evaluation* sites. record_evaluation_with_freshness resets diagnostics to empty on Changed but keeps the old ones on Unchanged (early cutoff). A site that omits the setter therefore drops warnings after a change and replays stale ones after a cutoff. unfold.rs discards the runtime sink entirely (see finding .1). Mechanism today: data field plus convention plus tests (harness_cache/eval_cached_diagnostics.rs).

findings.statement: Every subsystem showed the same shape: a correct helper is extracted and adopted at 3 of N sites, leaving N-3 inline copies that drift (cell_eval_ctx 4/72, journal helper 5/56, emit quintet 5/6, signatures_common half-finished dedup). The systemic cost is that an extraction without an adoption sweep plus a guard against new inline copies does not remove the next-change cost; it adds a second convention.

The attributed gmsh producer forbade vertex-merging repair while its only real caller fed raw unwelded OCCT tessellation, and the tetgen segfault was uncatchable; the mitigation was a scope-narrowing gate. Proposed a Rust-side watertightness preflight degrading to the plain producer, then attribution-aware repair. Verify which landed and whether the gate is still the mechanism.
findings.evidence: Both proposed remedies have landed and the gate is no longer the mechanism. Commit 3c5dbd2a99 (2026-07-11, #4876) added the Rust-side mesh_boundary.rs::preflight_watertight_surface. It returns GeometryError::MeshContractViolation instead of reaching tetgen. Commit cc76a78187 (2026-07-13, xi #5116) makes mesh_surface_to_volume_with_attribution always weld via repair_surface_mesh_with_correspondence when surface_needs_weld is true. That is attribution-aware repair that keeps input-node correspondence. It re-runs the preflight on the welded result and degrades to the plain producer on failure; this was read at the current tree. The behavioural guard is crates/reify-kernel-conformance/tests/occt_gmsh_attributed_conformance.rs::occt_box_attributed_volume_preserves_face_attribution, which runs real OCCT tessellation through the attributed producer.

findings.statement: execute_realization_ops (~1,794 lines) held a ~200-line cache-hit short-circuit that must remember to emulate every side effect of the main op loop — obligations implicit, not typed; three bugs clustered there (4349 double-insert, 3437 false hit, a perf regression); 11 task ids cited inside one function; ~24-parameter signature caused 11+ thread-new-arg fix commits. Proposed: RealizationOpsInput struct, probe_realization_cache extraction, KernelHandle re-key (#4351, done).
findings.evidence: The cache-hit short-circuit is now Engine::probe_realization_cache (task 5059 eta, done). Its obligations are pinned by five tests in engine_build/tests.rs: probe_realization_cache_primary_hit_applies_full_side_effect_set, _guard_requires_terminal_named_and_tol, _falls_back_to_brep_and_honors_tol_partial_order, _cold_warm_side_effect_set_parity, _debug_asserts_no_entry_at_cache_served_handle. The cross-kernel false-hit class was closed by the KernelHandle re-key (#4351, done). The ~24-parameter signature is now RealizationOpsInput::new (14 core args) plus with_* setters and RealizationOutputs. docs/invariants.md INV-BUILD-3 = enforced(test). Separately, the function itself grew from the ~1,794 lines the survey measured to 2,317 lines (re-measured by brace-matched span); that is reported as a new h4 finding, not as this one.

findings.statement: Version-id handling had three conventions: raw allocate-and-bump duplicated verbatim at 5 sites; a private current_eval_version() that engine_admin.rs could not call and so re-implemented as next_version_id.saturating_sub(1) with different edge semantics. Per-build reset invariants (feature_tag_table & co.) were hand-copied 3-line blocks at 4 entry points with no structural guarantee for a 5th table (proposed reset_per_build_state with exhaustive destructure).

findings.evidence: Commit a7ab9dce73 (feat(4954) step-2) makes the entity.rs MemberDecl::Let arm emit a Type::Geometry ValueCellDecl for each top-level geometry let, alongside its RealizationDecl, so build_combined_param_let_graph can link the node. Geometry-list lets (#5385) likewise emit a List<Geometry> cell. Residual: guarded geometry lets still emit no value cell, and INV-EVAL-5 is still 'proposed' with the #4952 no-stale-Undef checker as its interim guard (docs/invariants.md). The new cost in the same code is reported as a separate finding: let-kind classification is recomputed in every pass.

findings.statement: catch_unwind boundaries wrapped only the body-inline fallback; the primary compute-dispatch path had none and the FEA trampoline rested on ~30 panic!-based Value-shape asserts, so the CLI could crash the whole process on malformed/Undef inputs (GUI saved only by engine_lock's poison-safe wrapper). Proposed catch_unwind at invoke_compute_trampoline -> ComputeOutcome::Failed, then a Result-based extract_* refactor.
findings.evidence: invoke_compute_trampoline now lives in crates/reify-eval/src/engine_compute.rs (impl crate::Engine). It wraps the ComputeFn call in std::panic::catch_unwind and maps a panic to ComputeOutcome::Failed with the payload text. A `#[cfg(panic = "abort")] compile_error!` guards against a profile that would make catch_unwind a no-op. Landed in 362c383665 (task #5079, 2026-07-06). Both run_compute_dispatch and dispatch_compute_node route through it. A sibling gap on the plain cell-eval path is reported separately as finding .5.

findings.statement: The LSP dropped Indeterminate results at diagnostics.rs so FEA constraint violations produced no editor diagnostics — the same meaningless-pass shape as the CLI bugs — with no documented trampoline-free posture and no locking test. findings.evidence: Read compute_diagnostics_with_state's doc (sections '## Engine posture: deliberately NO compute trampolines' and '## Compile-time checker') and the test module at this tree. A documented posture exists (doc landed in 42b9c4e7bd), it is locked by the test fea_bearing_constraint_produces_no_false_violation_or_false_pass (probes every target in ALL_PRODUCTION_COMPUTE_TARGETS on both entry points, with an anti-vacuity check that each target is registrable), and Indeterminate FEA constraints are no longer silent: they get an INFORMATION diagnostic with code 'fea-not-evaluated' (introduced from b13344ed72 / 1ef585d9ab, task 5078), pinned by four fea_hint_* tests. Residual, reported as tooling.5 rather than as this prior: the test-only stateless compute_diagnostics still emits nothing for Indeterminate.

refuted.why: Ran `cargo tree --offline -p reify-audit -e normal,build --prefix none`. Read reify-test-support/Cargo.toml, including its features and the comment on reify-expr. Read reify-audit/Cargo.toml. Reproduced the 21-crate figure by walking cargo metadata with optional edges included. — The central claim is false. reify-test-support's reify-eval, reify-constraints and reify-expr dependencies are optional, behind the eval-helpers and containment-doubles features, and reify-audit depends on it without those features. The real normal+build closure of reify-audit is 10 workspace crates: ast, build-utils, builtins, compiler, config, core, ir, syntax, test-support, tree-sitter-reify. It does not include reify-eval, solver-elastic, any kernel, fdm or shell-extract. The 21 comes from counting optional edges. The cost the finding describes was already removed: test-support's Cargo.toml documents the gating, which brought the audit build from 185 to 130 crates. The leftover, a compiler-stack closure for 3 std-only names, is real but far smaller than claimed, and #6356 owns it.

synthesis.method: Payoff = severity x breadth x verdict, one rule applied to every ranked entry and never overridden by seat order: severity high=3, medium=2, low=1; breadth 1 when every measured site is inside the anchor's file, 2 when the measurements name several files inside one crate or one surface (one of: a crate, scripts/, tests/infra, gui/src-tauri, gui/src), 3 when they cross crates or surfaces (Rust+.ri, Rust+TS, bash+Python, docs+code); verdict confirmed=1, weakened=0.5, unverified=0.5 (the recovered engine_constraints/occt/engine_eval/engine_demand findings whose skeptic was lost to the usage cap, and p20, which no seat re-checked and which observation.unchecked should list). Breadth is read off each finding's statement and measurements by one script (synth2/rank.py: distinct crate paths, crate names and basenames resolved against git ls-files), with hand corrections where the text names modules without a file suffix (f263 15 files read Engine fields -> 2; f210 SingleKernelHolder in reify-geometry vs the trait in reify-ir -> 3; f69 four tokenizers in three reify-eval files -> 2; f2 elastic_static+modal_ops -> 2; f180 loop_closure+snapshot -> 2; f111 test file + harness-layout-lib private names -> 2; f137 verify.sh text pinned by 56 tests/infra members -> 3; f285 lib.rs summary parsed in ptodo/pdoccover/pdcheck/pcite -> 2; f70 handle.rs+lib.rs -> 2 as the critic measured; f324 24 modules of one crate -> 2) and for priors read off their statements (p2 two crates -> 3; p3 engine.rs+commands -> 2; p4 debug_server+AppState -> 2; p17 cache.rs+record_evaluation callers -> 2; p18 CLI/GUI/LSP entry points -> 3; p20 repo-wide -> 3). outcomes.note: The structure is real and the headline numbers reproduce. The 24-module SCC has exactly the named membership and 95,192 raw lines in the top-level files. The 3-module SCC {compute_targets, selector_vocabulary_v2, topology_selectors} also exists. All 13 sites exist in production code before each file's cfg(test) line. The predicate use counts match (8/7/4/4/3) and the file sizes are right (engine_eval is 15,306 lines by wc, one off). Three parts of the characterization do not hold. (1) dirty.rs:282 -> engine_fixpoint::run_unified_pass_seeded is not an upward edge. engine_fixpoint imports only cache and deps. Removing this edge leaves the SCC unchanged, and with it kept, dirty falls out of the SCC once the other sites are cut. (2) 'Nearly all pure predicates' is overstated. expand_solver_position_expr mutates an expr and pushes diagnostics. realize_sub_override_handles takes &mut kernels. run_unified_pass_seeded is the Kahn core. Only the geometry_ops predicates, is_optimized_userfn_cell and sub_refs_in_op are clean predicates. (3) Moving the proposed 9 helpers does not dissolve the SCC. With the 6 module-pair edges those moves remove cut, a 5-module SCC remains: engine_admin, engine_build, engine_edit, engine_eval and geometry_ops. It remains because geometry_ops -> engine_build::realize_sub_override_handles, which the next_change does not move. Cutting all 13 still leaves a cache<->deps 2-cycle (cache.rs:13 uses deps::DependencyTrace, deps.rs:12 uses cache::NodeId) and an engine_admin/engine_edit/engine_eval 3-cycle. The statement does not mention either. The refactor would shrink the SCC from 24 to about 5 modules, not remove the layering problem.

outcomes.note: All claims hold at a030ee75. snapshot.rs::value_for and loop_closure.rs::resolve_joint_value implement the same order: direct binding, coupling follows parent, fixed sentinel, range midpoint. wrap_jointvalue_for_joint has the same 7-arm match as the pub(crate) loop_closure::value_for_joint, with the same coupling-parent sub-match. snapshot.rs already imports joint_range_midpoint from loop_closure, so the shared helper is reachable. The copies diverge on multi-DOF. snapshot's value_for keeps only JointValue::Scalar from the midpoint and returns None otherwise, so an unbound planar joint, or a spherical one (whose midpoint is the identity quaternion), makes the snapshot Undef. loop_closure resolves the same joint to Planar/Sphere/Cyl. One small difference: value_for returns a direct binding as a raw Value, while loop_closure converts it through jointvalue_from_bound_value. That does not weaken the claim. The test doc for snapshot_with_unbound_planar_returns_undef says joint_range_midpoint returns None for planar and defers the fix to #2670. That is false: joint_range_midpoint has a Planar arm returning Some(Planar([mx,my,mθ])), and a loop_closure test asserts [0.5,0.5,π/2]. Task 2670 has status done, and its deliverables include the planar finite-difference fallback. The comment in wrap_midpoint_for_joint (line ~1493) repeats the same stale claim. outcomes.note:
The structure is real. Four top-level branches each carry their own spawn and PASS/FAIL recording. The helpers do reach branch state through globals: _ra_skip_engine rewrites _h2_discovered_list, _ra_skip_state_write reads `failures`, and _ra_partial_failed_names reads _H2_WORKDIR. The 6 spawn sites, 5 RESULT: FAIL sites and the per-branch coverage counts for sanitize, fail-detail, H3 and retry all reproduce. One caveat on the coverage count: the final backstop `_ra_interrupt_if_worktree_gone` at line 2057 runs after every branch, subset included, so the 2/4 for worktree-gone only holds for the per-iteration check. The code comment calling the backstop 'common to both pool and legacy' understates this.

The 'follow-up commits porting a feature to another branch' measurement does not hold, though. Only 3ef7845834 (collect FAIL-detail on the subset retry path) and 7439d071b2 (sanitize the subset re-emit) are ports into the subset branch. 746b4474ea introduced the git-env scrub as a new concern and wrapped all six spawns in that one commit, so it is a uniform rollout and the opposite of a branch-by-branch gap. 889910ef1d extends the _ra_collect_fail_detail sed chain to match _ra_emit_sanitized, so its 'second site' is a second function, not a second branch. The count is therefore about 2 of 44, not 4 of 44.

The omissions also look largely deliberate rather than accidental. The subset branch's header says it never consults _h3_exclude and runs a single attempt. The H9 branch says it deliberately ignores _h3_exclude. This weakens the 'nothing structural ensures a new concern reaches every branch' framing, because test_infra_git_env_isolation's end-to-end probe covers scrub propagation.

The next_change scenario is plausible, but its weight is overstated by the miscounted evidence.

seats.area_health: Read in full: the production half of both size-alarm files — modal_ops.rs lines 1-4547 (the #[cfg(test)] module, 8,288 lines, was indexed and its import list and assertion patterns sampled) and elastic_static.rs lines 1-5800 (the 9,538-line test module was indexed and its call sites sampled). Neither file counts as read fully, because most of each file's lines are tests. I followed seams only far enough to anchor claims: buckling.rs's readers, reify_ir::arg_acceptance, solver_progress and the engine's cancel wiring, assembly::test_support, and the .ri result declarations. The numerics are careful and heavily tested. The next-change cost is in how the trampolines talk to everything around them. (1) Each trampoline decodes stdlib Values (ElasticMaterial, *Options, loads) with its own ad-hoc readers, and failure policy varies by file: Result in elastic_static, panic! in buckling, silent 0.0 in modal_ops. The canonical dimension-checked reader (reify_ir::arg_acceptance) is used at only a few positions. (2) Result structs (ElasticResult, ModalResult, Mode) are spelled out field by field at several producer sites, and the Rust producers write fields the .ri declarations do not declare. (3) Cancellation has two channels, and the trampolines split between them. (4) elastic_static's single 1,170-line trampoline function handles five independent axes inline. modal_ops.rs bundles four compute targets plus a face-name BC-realization subsystem under a module doc that describes only one of them. About 46-47% of the production lines in both files are comments, and much of that prose answers reviewers. I measured drift in several of those comments (stale mesh sizes, a deleted function cited as the 'mirror', '10 args' over a 14-parameter function, '6 fields' over 7). In-file tests import 47 names, 30 of them fully private, so the tests pin the module's internal factoring.

The static path also auto-clamps a coordinate 'root' face via a string match. Candidate SPOT/orthogonality finding for the constraints or analysis cross-seat. 2) INV-PD-2 (docs/legibility/design-invariants.md) names `reify-audit --pattern PVAC` as enforcement, but no PVAC detector exists in crates/reify-audit (reify-audit seat). 3) The cancellation dual channel spans engine_eval.rs (fresh per-dispatch handle, cancelled only from a dead branch), engine_compute.rs (installs Engine.active_solve_cancel thread-locally), solver_progress.rs and gui/src-tauri/src/engine.rs.
